## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The TTL change and its comment match. The new `Cache.set` breaks the module's case-insensitive key rule, so values written under mixed-case keys can never be read back. This should be fixed before merge.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — `set` stores the key as given (`self._store[key] = ...`), but `get` always looks up `key.lower()` (app/cache.py:17). The comment at app/cache.py:14-15 says "every path into _store lower-cases the key first", and `set` skips that step. After `c.set("Alpha", 1)`, both `c.get("Alpha")` and `c.get("alpha")` return `None`, because the entry sits under `"Alpha"` and lookups use `"alpha"`. Could you store under `key.lower()` and add a test that calls `set` with a mixed-case key? The current round-trip test at tests/test_cache.py:12 writes the lowercase key `"alpha"`, so it can't catch this. — Any caller that writes a mixed-case key always gets a cache miss. `get` only deletes `key.lower()`, so those entries are never cleared and stay in `_store` forever. Writing `"Alpha"` and `"alpha"` also leaves two separate entries, which is the problem the comment warns about.

## Strengths
- The comment at app/cache.py:7 ("Entries expire 300 seconds after they are written") matches the new `DEFAULT_TTL = 300` on app/cache.py:8.
- `test_entries_expire` (tests/test_cache.py:21-27) uses a fake clock, so it doesn't depend on real time. It patches the same `time.monotonic` attribute that `cache.py` reads, so it really tests expiry in both `set` and `get`.
